content:
olga: Heads-up — seeing a weird backlog in ap-southeast1 warmpools, lots of tiny GPU pods pending. Not typical.
ben: Link to dashboard? :eyes:
mike: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cluster/az-capacity — node utilization in ap-southeast1b is 98% for GPU nodes, others 40-60%.
olga: kubectl output shows `InsufficientGPU` but there are free GPUs in the region. I'm pretty sure it's AZ affinity/taint related.
akshay: Can you paste the pending pod list? Also any taints on nodes? 
olga: pasted snippet:
```
NAME                         READY STATUS    RESTARTS AGE   NODE           REASON
trainer-xyz-7d9f             0/1   Pending   0      12m  <none>         InsufficientGPU
small-infer-abc-5f2          0/1   Pending   0      9m   <none>         InsufficientGPU
```
Nodes:
```
NODE          AZ     GPU    TAINTS
gpu-a-12      a      8      gpu-exclusive:NoSchedule
gpu-b-11      b      2      <none>
gpu-c-03      b      4      gpu-dedicated:NoSchedule
``` 
mike: ah — a lot of long-lived dedicated workloads were scheduled into b due to earlier topology constraints. Other AZs have capacity but our scheduler avoids cross-AZ placement because of `preferSameAZ: true` in the KubeScheduler config.
ben: That config was added last quarter to reduce cross-AZ NVLink ineffs. But it's causing fragmentation when AZ b gets sticky.
olga: Short-term mitigation: can we relax preferSameAZ to `prefer` -> `avoid` for small pods? Maybe add policy: tiny pods can binpack across AZs.
akshay: We can do a canary: update schedulerpolicy for `small-pod-class` with `topologySpread` -> allow inter-AZ, rollout to ap-southeast1 only. Need an escape hatch to revert in 10m.
infra-bot: deploy-plan posted: /deploys/scheduler-policy/2026-03-21T12:10Z — canary to ap-southeast1 only. @akshay to trigger.
mike: Before that, quick temporary step: signal autoscaler to add 2 nodes in ap-southeast1c and increase `preemptionGracePeriod` to 30s so small jobs get evicted faster into free slots.
akshay: I don't love adding capacity without addressing placement — costs go up. Suggest: 1) canary policy to relax AZ bias for pods <1 GPU, 2) run defrag job to cordon and schedule small pods onto underutilized nodes, 3) autoscaler bump only if defrag fails.
ben: Defrag job idea: a controller that finds underutilized nodes and migrates tiny pods for 15 minutes, then releases. We had something like that for CPU last year. Any abort criteria? network egress spikes, or >10% latency increase.
olga: Also we need to watch tenancy: some nodes have `gpu-dedicated` taint for enterprise customers. Defrag must respect taints + node affinity labels.
akshay: I'll prepare the canary patch and the defrag runbook. Plan timeline: patch at 12:10, monitor 12:10-12:40, trigger defrag at 12:45 if still >10 pending pods. Rollback 12:55 if error.
infra-bot: scheduled: canary patch will be applied in 5m. Monitoring alerts: `pending_gpus > 20` and `p95_pod_schedule_time > 120s` are active.
mike: Also add a quick alert to cost channel: if we spin up >3 extra nodes in the region, flag finance. Want visibility.
ben: I'll draft the short PR with schedulerpolicy JSON and the defrag runbook. @olga can you capture the pending pod selector so defrag targets only pods with gpu requests <= 1?
olga: Yup — selector: `spec.resources.requests['nvidia.com/gpu'] <= 1 && !metadata.labels['enterprise-locked']`. Pasting into runbook.
akshay: Great. If canary shows improved scheduling and no perf regressions, we'll roll the policy region-wide and follow-up with an autoscaler tuning to prefer cross-AZ binpack for tiny pods.
olga: Thanks all. I'll watch the canary and post updates here. :thumbsup:
